Singapore | hq_location = 20 Martin Road | key_people = | industry = [[Food and Beverage]] | area_served = {{flat list| * [[Hong Kong]] * [[Indonesia]] * [[Singapore]] }} | products = {{flat list| * [[Coffee|Coffee beverages]] * Baked goods }} | revenue = | operating_income = | net_income = | num_employees = | parent = Dhunseri Group{{cite web|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/food/dhunseri-group-takes-over-twelve-cupcakes/articleshow/56753170.cms|title=Dhunseri Group takes over Twelve Cupcakes |publisher=Economic Times India|date=24 January 2017|accessdate=15 March 2017}} | footnotes = }} '''Twelve Cupcakes''' was a [[Singapore]] based chain of cupcakery selling [[Cupcake|cupcakes]]. It was [[Co-Founder|co-founded]] by Singaporean DJ [[Daniel Ong]] and actress Jamie Teo in 2011, before being sold to Dhunseri Group in 2017. It ceased operations on 29 October 2025. ==Name== According to Ong, the cupcakery is named "for 12 strikes in a perfect game of bowling, 12 months in a year, 12 numbers on a clock and of course, the 12 holes in a typical baking tray".{{cite web|url=http://www.thestar.com.my/business/sme/2014/01/15/a-piece-of-cake-singapore-celebrities-open-third-cupcake-outlet-in-klang-valley-to-woo-dessert-love/|title=Singapore celebrities open third cupcake outlet in Klang Valley|work=The Star|date=14 January 2014|accessdate=3 April 2016}} ==History== [[File:Twelve Cupcakes cupcakes.jpg|200px|thumbnail|right|Twelve Cupcakes cupcakes in a box of 3.]] In 2011, Ong and Teo started Twelve Cupcakes with Teo having created the recipes of all the cupcakes sold in the stores. The cupcakes sold were made to suit to the Asian palate, which are less sweet compared to western cupcakes.{{cite web|url=http://www.twelvecupcakes.com/images/Jan'12_Guardian.pdf|title=Jamie Teo and the Magical story of Mr Handsome's Twelve Cupcakes|publisher=Guardian Feeling|date=January 2012|accessdate=18 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140704145855/http://twelvecupcakes.com/images/Jan'12_Guardian.pdf|archive-date=4 July 2014|url-status=dead}} The first outlet of Twelve Cupcakes was opened at United Square Shopping Mall, in [[Novena, Singapore|Novena]], which started with two service staff. The company then expanded and opened three more outlets during the first year of operations and sold over three million cupcakes in July 2011.{{cite web|url=http://poachedmag.com/2013/03/30/interview-supermum-cupcake-queen-jaime-teo/|title=[Interview] Cupcake Queen Jaime Teo|publisher=Poached Mag|date=30 March 2013|access-date=18 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141218175428/http://poachedmag.com/2013/03/30/interview-supermum-cupcake-queen-jaime-teo/|archive-date=18 December 2014|url-status=dead}} In 2013, Twelve Cupcakes expanded internationally, opening outlets in Jakarta, Taipei, [[Kuala Lumpur]], and Hong Kong.{{Cite news |date=June 2016 |title=Sweet Deal |url=https://static1.businesstimes.com.sg/s3fs-public/attachment/2016/04/27/BT_SMEMAYJUNE2016_05.pdf}} In 2014, Twelve Cupcakes started a new dessert cafe known as Dulce and Sucre by Twelve Cupcakes at [[Orchard Gateway]], where it sold freshly baked loaves, whoopie pies, push up cakes, parfaits, puddings, tiramisus, crunchies, coffees and other desserts.{{cite web |date=4 July 2014 |title=Dulce and Sucre Opens + F&B Entrepreneurship Lessons With Daniel Ong |url=https://sg.news.yahoo.com/dulce-sucre-opens-f-b-032200469.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141218175855/https://sg.news.yahoo.com/dulce-sucre-opens-f-b-032200469.html |archive-date=18 December 2014 |access-date=18 December 2014 |publisher=Yahoo Singapore}}{{cite web |date=2 May 2014 |title=Dulce And Sucre – Twelve Cupcakes Opens A New Dessert Cafe |url=http://danielfooddiary.com/2014/05/02/dulcesucre/?amp;utm_medium=rss& |accessdate=18 December 2014 |publisher=Daniel Food Diary}} It converted to a Twelve Cupcakes outlet in 2015.{{Citation needed|date=October 2025}} On 24 January 2017, after the divorce of Ong and Teo in late 2016, the chain was sold to Dhunseri Group, which acquired it for [[Singapore dollar|S$]]2.5 million.{{cite web|url=http://www.todayonline.com/business/twelve-cupcakes-sold-indian-tea-company|title=Twelve Cupcakes sold to Indian tea company for S$2.5 million|publisher=Channel NewsAsia|date=24 January 2017|accessdate=15 March 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Goh |first1=Kenneth |title=Indian tea company buys over Twelve Cupcakes chain |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/lifestyle/food/indian-tea-company-buys-over-twelve-cupcakes-chain |website=The Straits Times |access-date=10 December 2021 |date=24 January 2017}} At the [[point of sale]], the company had 17 outlets in Singapore and more than 10 outlets in Jakarta, Taipei and Hong Kong that were run by franchise partners.{{Cite news |date=2017-01-24 |title=Indian tea company buys over Twelve Cupcakes chain |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/lifestyle/food/indian-tea-company-buys-over-twelve-cupcakes-chain |access-date=2025-10-31 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}} Since 2023 until its closure in 2025, Twelve Cupcakes reported consecutive years of widening net loss and shrinking revenue annually.{{Cite web |last=Lim |first=Therese Soh, Chloe |date=2025-10-30 |title=Twelve Cupcakes shutters, bakery chain in provisional liquidation |url=https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/singapore/twelve-cupcakes-shutters-bakery-chain-provisional-liquidation |access-date=2025-10-30 |website=The Business Times |language=en}} On 29 October 2025, Twelve Cupcakes ceased operations and was placed under provisional liquidation.{{Cite news |date=2025-10-30 |title=Twelve Cupcakes ceases operations as company is placed under provisional liquidation |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/twelve-cupcakes-ceases-operations-after-being-placed-under-provisional-liquidation |access-date=2025-10-30 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}} The management did not notify its staff about the impending closure, while the union was notified the day before, and left 80 workers unemployed.{{Cite web |title='Very, very unfair': Twelve Cupcakes staff blindsided by abrupt closure |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/twelve-cupcakes-staff-abrupt-closure-workers-5435486 |access-date=2025-10-31 |website=CNA |language=en}} Assistance was provided by Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union to the affected employees was provided in form of financial aid, grocery vouchers, and job placements with other companies. In March 2026, after negotiations between the union and the liquidator, the former employees received a portion of their salaries owed.{{Cite web |title=Former Twelve Cupcakes workers to get part of unpaid salaries after months of talks: Union |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/twelve-cupcakes-workers-get-unpaid-salary-payouts-fdawu-union-6028916 |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=CNA |language=en}} ==Products and stores== Twelve Cupcakes features 60 flavours of [[cupcake]]s sold in its stores, with a standard '12 Everyday Flavours' and 50 specials sold on a rotational basis. A new flavour of cupcake is also launched monthly.{{cn|date=June 2023}} Twelve Cupcakes new dine-in cafe outlet, Dulce and Sucre, offers a wider variety of menu items, with coffees, whoopie pies, push up cakes, parfaits and other baked items.{{cite web|url=http://www.moneydigest.sg/dulce-and-sucre-buy-1-get-1-free-sweet-treats/|title=Dulce and Sucre: Buy 1 Get 1 Free Sweet Treats|publisher=Money Digest Singapore|date=5 July 2015|accessdate=3 April 2016}} Twelve Cupcakes had its presence in Indonesia before ceasing operations in 2018.{{Citation needed|date=April 2026}}{{Citation needed|date=April 2026}} At its time of closure, the chain operated 21 stores located in 2 locations with 1 in Hong Kong and 20 in Singapore.{{Cite news |date=2025-10-30 |title=Twelve Cupcakes ceases operations as company is placed under provisional liquidation |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/twelve-cupcakes-ceases-operations-after-being-placed-under-provisional-liquidation |access-date=2025-10-30 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}{{Cite web |title=Cake Shop Location in Central |url=https://twelvecupcakes.com.hk/pages/store-location |access-date=2025-10-30 |website=Twelve Cupcakes HK |language=en}} ==Controversy== ===Singapore Press Holdings=== In 2012, [[Singapore Press Holdings]] (SPH) demanded payment from the cupcakery for reproducing its articles online. The cupcakery put up articles written about their business on [[Facebook]], [[Twitter]] and the company's website, which infringes the copyright of SPH and violates copyright law in Singapore.{{cite web|url=https://www.techinasia.com/twelve-cupcakes-shares-articles-about-itself-on-facebook-sph-allegedly-demands-payment/|title=Twelve Cupcakes displays articles about itself on website; SPH demands payment|publisher=Tech in Asia|date=6 July 2012|accessdate=18 December 2014}} ===Underpayment of foreign staff=== Twelve Cupcakes was accused of underpaying its foreign workers between 2017 and 2019 by the [[Ministry of Manpower (Singapore)|Ministry of Manpower]]. When the workers were supposed to be paid salaries ranging from $2,200 to $2,600, the actual salaries paid were lower at $1,400 to $2,050. Initially, the salaries were paid in reduced amounts, before changing tactics to pay the actual salaries with a portion needing to be returned to the company. Twelve Cupcakes was first charged for its offences on 1 October 2020, before pleading guilty on 10 December. Twelve Cupcakes was fined $119,500 on 12 January 2021 for its offences.{{cite web |last1=Tang |first1=Louisa |title=Twelve Cupcakes accused of underpaying 8 foreign employees over 2 years July 2021}} After the company was sold to Dhunseri Group, the underpayment of the company's workers continued from 2017 to 2018 under the new management. In January 2021, the company was fined $119,500.{{Cite news |date=2021-01-12 |title=Twelve Cupcakes fined $119,500 over multiple counts of underpaying its employees |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/courts-crime/twelve-cupcakes-fined-119500-over-multiple-counts-of-underpaying-its?ref=inline-article |access-date=2025-10-30 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}} Due to these instances of underpayment, the Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union (a union affiliated to [[National Trades Union Congress]]) announced on 16 February 2021 plans to unionise the company to make sure workers are fairly represented and to work with the company's management on better employment practices. These plans were being set out as early as late 2020 with the management and employees of the company informed. The company was successfully unionised 10 days later with a secret ballot by the Ministry of Manpower, with majority of the workers voting overwhelmingly for the arrangement.{{cite web |title=Plans to extract: Twelve Cupcakes was a Singapore based chain of cupcakery selling cupcakes. It was co-founded by Singaporean DJ Daniel Ong and actress Jamie Teo in 2011, before being sold to Dhunseri Group in 2017. It ceased operations on 29 October 2025.
